title: console-observability-triage-scratchpad
content:
Quick scratchpad for console/observability triage (notes to self).

Context: customer ACME reported dashboards showing 30-60s spikes in query latency on 2026-03-03 (see INF-4278). Console metrics show intermittent surge in compute latency and some 500s from backend route /v1/metrics/fetch. Need to collect repro steps, short-term mitigation, and follow-ups.

Observed / immediate notes:
- 2026-03-03 10:14-10:42 UTC: multiple alerts from SLO monitor (p95 latency breaching).
- Affected dashboards: "obs-latency-overview", "model-p95-by-route".
- Error pattern: spikes correlated with larger-than-usual batched requests from a single tenant (ACME).
- Backend errors: spike in 500 responses from metrics API (internal) — logs show timeout to redis-cache host redis-prod-3.
- Not consistently reproducible in staging.

Repro steps (candidate):
1) Simulate batched traffic: send mixed-size batch of inference meta-requests via loadtest script (scripts/loadtest/latency-spike.sh) pointed at metrics fetch route.
2) Observe console dashboard and backend logs around redis cache hits/misses.
3) Re-run with cache disabled (feature flag) to see if latency pattern changes.

Hypotheses:
- H1: Redis cluster transiently overloaded (connection saturation) causing timeouts and cascading backpressure to metrics pipeline.
- H2: A recent console deploy (PR #742) introduced a change in query pattern that increases multi-tenant batch fanout and causes heavy KV cache churn.
- H3: Routing policy change sent more requests to a smaller pool (dedicated), causing capacity hotspots.

Immediate actions (today):
- [ ] Talk to infra on-call (Evan) to check redis-prod-3 metrics + connection pool stats. (owner: Evan, due: 2026-03-04)
- [ ] Roll back console PR #742 on a canary subset if infra indicates deploy-correlated spike. (owner: me / Priya, due: 2026-03-04)
- [ ] Add temporary alert to detect >10% 500s from /v1/metrics/fetch over 5m (owner: me, due: 2026-03-04).
- [ ] Ask CS to gather ACME's request logs for 2026-03-03 window (linked INF-4278). (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Create loadtest to mimic ACME traffic profile; run on staging to validate reproduction (owner: me, due: 2026-03-05).

Follow-ups / longer-term:
- Investigate connection pooling and timeouts for Redis client used by metrics pipeline; consider increasing pool or adding client-side backoff.
- Add KV cache telemetry to dashboards: per-tenant miss rates + connection saturation.
- Add per-route capacity routing metrics; check if routing rules recently changed (CON-915).
- Postmortem if rollback or mitigation required; include timeline and mitigation steps.

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- When running loadtest, use header X-Tenant-ID: acme-inc to mimic routing rules.
- Watch for correlation with autoscaler events (scale up/scale down) — maybe scale flapping.
- Check if quantization/large-model batched requests cause memory pressure on serving nodes which then slow instrumentation pipelines.

Conversation snippets / cribbed links:
- Slack: @evan "redis-prod-3 showed connection spikes at 10:12 UTC, threads queued" (see Slack thread).
- PR 742 changed how we batch metric queries (grouped by tenant), might increase TTL churn.

TODO (ordered):
1) Contact on-call infra and get redis metrics + recent restarts.
2) Create temporary alert and post in #console-ops.
3) Start staging loadtest using ACME profile.
4) If reproduced, rollback PR 742 canary.
5) Draft short email to ACME CS explaining we are investigating and providing ETA.

Open questions:
- Is ACME traffic pattern unique (very large batches) or did something change on our side?
- Are there any recent infra changes around redis cluster (ops window) that align with timestamps?
- Could this be related to Dedicated routing policy change last week? (check CON-915)

End-of-day notes (2026-03-03):
- Ran a basic loadtest — partial reproduction with 30% p95 spike when simulating ACME-sized batches, but not full 60s spikes. Redis metrics show elevated blocked clients at peak.
- Reached out to Evan; infra investigating and will consider adding replica and increasing maxclients.
- Filed INF-4278 with initial timeline and logs.

Next update: 2026-03-04 morning — coordinate with infra and CS, decide rollback vs mitigation.

(Handy references)
- metrics fetch route: /v1/metrics/fetch
- loadtest script: tools/loadtests/obs-batch-sim.py
- related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/742
- JIRA: INF-4278, CON-915
plain_text_preview: Personal triage scratchpad for console/observability issues (ACME latency spike). Includes hypotheses, immediate actions, repro steps, and next steps.
